newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan June crude steel output up 5.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan June crude steel output up 5.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Japan's crude steel production in June was 8.71 million tonnes, up 5.6 percent from a year earlier, the Japan Iron and Steel Federation said on Tuesday.
Japan's crude steel output in the first six months of calendar 1997 totalled 52.68 million tonnes, up 8.0 percent from a year earlier.
Crude steel production in the April to June period, Japan's first fiscal quarter, rose 7.7 percent from the same period last year to 26.77 million tonnes, the steel federation said.
Year-on-year, crude steel output rose in June for the ninth straight month, the federation said, though it fell 5.6 percent compared to May.

Crude steel output in the April-June quarter rose for the third straight quarter on a year-on-year basis and exceeded 26 million tonnes for the first time since totalling 26.44 million in the 1995 April-June period.

June output of tin plate was 132,200 tonnes, down 0.2 percent year-on-year and down 6.3 percent month-on-month, bringing output to 772,200 tonnes in the January-June period, down 1.7 percent from a year earlier, the federation said.
Output of tin plate in the April-June period rose 1.6 percent from a year earlier to 394,400 tonnes.
Production of galvanised steel sheet in June rose 12.6 percent from a year earlier to 1.06 million tonnes, and first-half output rose 13.0 percent to 6.41 million tonnes, it said.
Galvanised steel sheet output in April-June rose 11.7 percent to 3.20 million tonnes.
